newsitem.title: USA: MCI-led group wins US Postal network management deal.
newsitem.headline: MCI-led group wins US Postal network management deal.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. said Wednesday the U.S. Postal Service awarded an MCI-led group a five-year contract to manage its telecommunications network.
MCI said the contract, the largest it has ever won, has a guaranteed value of at least $100 million and a potential value of up to $3 billion.
The deal calls for the partners to provide the Postal Service with an array of telecommunications services
MCI, which is based in McLean, Va., was the lead contractor on the deal. Other suppliers on the contract team include Cisco Systems Inc. and Digital Equipment Corp.
The has two three-year renewal options that could allow the contract to run for up to 11 years, MCI said.
As part of the deal, MCI will establish and manage a telecommunications network to connect up to 34,000 Postal Service facilities.
MCI said the managed network operations will improve post office customer service by streamlining operations and creating mechanisms for providing new types of services.
The network will improve the Postal Service's access to data and information across multiple computer systems, provide centralized software distribution and help-desk technical support, MCI said.
"The MCI network will give us the availability and responsiveness we need to meet our customers' expectations," Rick Weirich, vice president of information services for the Postal Service, said.
